_about: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION SCRIPT. Hand-written text used ONLY for the three built-in synthetic sample bills when no recorded AI review (cache/manifest.json) is deployed. No AI model wrote this. Outcomes are not chosen here: which candidates exist and whether each is kept or dropped come from data/synthetic/<bill>/seed_manifest.json and are enforced by src/lib/demo.ts. Every answer still passes the same schema, number-guard, tone and Judge-rule checks as live AI output. {facts.<key>} placeholders are filled by code from the finding's code-computed facts, so no figure here is typed by hand.

auditor.claim: Line L001 bills {facts.days_billed} room days, but the bill's own dates give {facts.nights} nights, and code allows at most {facts.allowed_days} room days.
auditor.evidence_point: Room days billed exceed nights plus one by {facts.extra_days} day(s), worth {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: A room day that does not match the stay is charged at the full daily rate of {facts.daily_rate}.

defender.strongest_justification: The discharge summary narrative says discharge was ordered on 2026-08-04, but transport was unavailable and the patient stayed in the room overnight, leaving on 2026-08-05.
supporting_points: The free-text summary records the extra overnight in the room.
The structured discharge date is the order date, not the physical departure.
defender.what_would_confirm: The ward bed-occupancy log or gate pass showing departure on 2026-08-05.

judge.rationale: The narrative documents a real extra night in the room after the discharge order, which accounts for the additional room day.
judge.counter_argument: This charge appears to be explained by the discharge summary: the patient remained in the room one extra night while waiting for transport. It is shown for transparency and not counted.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Can you confirm the room was occupied until the morning of 2026-08-05?

auditor.claim: Line L003 prints {facts.printed_amount}, but its own quantity and rate give {facts.quantity_times_rate}.
auditor.evidence_point: Quantity {facts.quantity} at {facts.unit_rate} per day; the printed amount is higher by {facts.difference}.
auditor.why_it_matters: The bill contradicts its own figures, so the excess can be shown from the bill alone.

defender.strongest_justification: A surcharge or extra nursing shift might have been folded into this line during billing.
supporting_points: Hospitals sometimes merge add-on nursing charges into one line.
defender.what_would_confirm: A separate, itemised nursing surcharge entry with its own quantity and rate.

judge.rationale: No surcharge appears anywhere on the bill. The printed amount does not follow from the printed quantity and rate.
judge.counter_argument: The bill's own quantity and rate give {facts.quantity_times_rate}, not {facts.printed_amount}. Any extra charge should be its own line, so please correct this line by {facts.amount_at_stake}.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Please explain why line L003 is higher than its quantity times its rate, or correct it.

auditor.claim: Line L013 bills Azikaa tablets at {facts.billed_rate_per_unit} each, above the reference MRP of {facts.reference_mrp_per_unit} for this brand.
auditor.evidence_point: The billed brand matches a verified reference row; the excess over MRP is {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: A medicine should not be sold above the MRP printed on its pack.

defender.strongest_justification: The pharmacy may have issued a newer batch printed with a higher MRP than the reference value.
defender.what_would_confirm: The strip label or pharmacy issue slip showing the MRP printed on the pack that was issued.

judge.rationale: The bill prints no MRP and no batch, and the brand matches the verified reference row, so the higher rate is not explained.
judge.counter_argument: Unless the pack issued shows a higher printed MRP, the rate above {facts.reference_mrp_per_unit} per tablet should be refunded: {facts.amount_at_stake}.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: What MRP was printed on the Azikaa strips issued under line L013?

auditor.claim: Line L014 bills C-Tri ceftriaxone at {facts.billed_rate_per_unit} per vial, above both the reference MRP and the ceiling price including GST.
auditor.evidence_point: Billed above the reference-table MRP and the NPPA ceiling price including GST; the excess over the lower limit, {facts.binding_limit_per_unit} per vial, is {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: This medicine is price-controlled; a vial should not cost more than its ceiling price or MRP.

defender.strongest_justification: Preparation or handling of an injectable is sometimes added to the vial price.
supporting_points: Some hospitals add a mixing or administration charge to injections.
defender.what_would_confirm: A separate line for drug administration or preparation charges.

judge.rationale: No administration charge is shown, and any such charge should be a separate line, not part of the medicine's price.
judge.counter_argument: The medicine's own price cannot exceed its ceiling price or MRP. Please refund {facts.amount_at_stake} or show a separate, itemised administration charge.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Why is line L014 priced above the MRP and ceiling price for this vial?

auditor.claim: Lines L016 and L017 are the same normal saline bag on the same date and time.
auditor.evidence_point: {facts.copies_billed} identical copies billed; the repeat copy is {facts.amount_of_repeat_copies}.
auditor.why_it_matters: Identical entries at the same moment are a common double-entry error.

defender.strongest_justification: In sepsis, two bags can be started together as a fluid bolus.
supporting_points: Fluid resuscitation can use more than one bag at once.
defender.what_would_confirm: The nursing fluid chart showing two bags started at that time.

judge.rationale: Two bags at once is possible, but nothing in the documents shows it. This stays a question, not a proven error.
judge.counter_argument: Two identical lines at the same date and time usually mean one bag was entered twice. If the fluid chart shows one bag, please remove {facts.amount_at_stake}.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Does the nursing fluid chart show two saline bags started at that time?

auditor.claim: The admission and registration fee appears twice, on lines L018 and L019.
auditor.evidence_point: A one-time fee billed on {facts.lines_billed} lines ({facts.dates}); the repeat is {facts.amount_of_repeat_lines}.
auditor.why_it_matters: A registration fee is normally charged once per admission.

defender.strongest_justification: Some hospitals charge registration again when a patient moves between units, such as ICU to ward.
supporting_points: Unit transfers can trigger separate registration in some billing systems.
defender.what_would_confirm: The hospital's tariff showing a per-unit registration fee.

judge.rationale: A per-unit fee is not documented anywhere provided. Keep this as a question for the billing desk.
judge.counter_argument: There was one admission. Unless the tariff shows a separate fee per unit, the second registration fee of {facts.amount_at_stake} should be removed.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Why was the admission and registration fee charged twice for one admission?

clinical.summary_evidence: Echocardiography is not in investigations_documented, and the narrative states it is not listed and that no cardiac indication is documented.
clinical.reasoning: A billed echocardiogram with no mention anywhere in the summary should be supported by an order or report.

auditor.claim: Line L012 bills echocardiography with Doppler, but the discharge summary does not mention it.
auditor.evidence_point: Not in the structured investigations, and the narrative notes no cardiac indication. Amount billed: {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: A charge for a test the clinical record does not mention should be backed by an order or report.

defender.strongest_justification: Echocardiography is often done in sepsis to check heart function; the report may simply be missing from the summary.
supporting_points: Summaries do not always list every test.
defender.what_would_confirm: The echocardiography report or the doctor's order for it.

judge.rationale: The test is clinically plausible, but the documents provided do not support it. Keep it as a question, not a proven error.
judge.counter_argument: The summary specifically notes no cardiac indication. Please share the echo report or order; without it, {facts.amount_at_stake} should be reviewed.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Can you share the echocardiography report or order for line L012?

auditor.claim: Line L002 bills {facts.icu_days_billed} ICU days, but the discharge summary documents {facts.icu_days_documented_in_summary} ICU days.
auditor.why_it_matters: ICU days are among the most expensive lines on a bill.

defender.strongest_justification: The summary narrative says the patient had two ICU days followed by two HDU/step-down days, and the billing export groups all four critical-care days under one ICU line.
supporting_points: The free-text summary describes the step-down days explicitly.
The line description itself says the export groups ICU and HDU days.
defender.what_would_confirm: The bed-transfer log showing the ICU and HDU sequence.

judge.rationale: The documents explain the extra days as step-down care grouped under one billing code, so this is not a charge to question.
judge.counter_argument: This charge appears to be explained by the discharge summary: the extra days were HDU/step-down care billed under one critical-care code. It is shown for transparency and not counted.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Can the bed-transfer log confirm the ICU and HDU days billed under line L002?

auditor.claim: The bill's stated total is {facts.stated_total}, but its lines add up to {facts.sum_of_line_amounts}.
auditor.evidence_point: With a stated discount of {facts.stated_discount}, the expected total is {facts.expected_total}; the difference is {facts.difference}.
auditor.why_it_matters: The bill contradicts its own lines, so the gap can be shown from the bill alone.

defender.strongest_justification: An unlisted charge, such as a deposit adjustment or a late entry, may have been added at the total.
supporting_points: Late charges are sometimes added after the itemised list is printed.
defender.what_would_confirm: An itemised line for the additional amount.

judge.rationale: No line explains the gap. A charge that is not itemised cannot be checked.
judge.counter_argument: Every charge should appear as a line. Please itemise or remove the {facts.amount_at_stake} by which the total exceeds the sum of the lines.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Which charge explains the difference between the line items and the stated total?

auditor.claim: Line L009 bills Moxikem CV tablets at {facts.billed_rate_per_unit} each, above the reference MRP of {facts.reference_mrp_per_unit}.
auditor.evidence_point: The billed brand matches a verified reference row; the excess over MRP is {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: A medicine should not be sold above the MRP printed on its pack.

defender.strongest_justification: A newer batch with a higher printed MRP may have been issued.
defender.what_would_confirm: The pack label or pharmacy issue slip showing the printed MRP.

judge.rationale: No batch or MRP is printed on the bill, and the brand matches the verified reference row.
judge.counter_argument: Unless the issued pack shows a higher MRP, the rate above {facts.reference_mrp_per_unit} per tablet should be refunded: {facts.amount_at_stake}.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: What MRP was printed on the Moxikem CV strips issued under line L009?

auditor.claim: Line L001 bills {facts.days_billed} room days for a stay of {facts.nights} nights; code allows at most {facts.allowed_days}.
auditor.why_it_matters: Room days above the stay are charged at the full daily rate.

defender.strongest_justification: Some hospitals count both the admission day and the discharge day as room days.
defender.what_would_confirm: A record of a delayed departure after the discharge date.

judge.rationale: The allowance already counts nights plus one day, and the narrative notes no discharge delay.
judge.counter_argument: Even counting both the admission and discharge days, the stay allows fewer room days than billed. Please remove {facts.amount_at_stake} or show a delayed departure.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Why are more room days billed on line L001 than the stay allows?

clinical.summary_evidence: blood_products_documented is empty, and the narrative says no blood products are described in the clinical course.
clinical.reasoning: Two units of packed red cells would normally appear in the summary and in a transfusion record.

auditor.claim: Line L015 bills two units of packed red blood cells, but the summary says no blood products were given.
auditor.evidence_point: No blood products in the structured summary or the narrative. Amount billed: {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: Blood products are always recorded with a transfusion note and a blood-bank issue slip.

defender.strongest_justification: Blood may have been cross-matched and reserved for surgery, and the reservation billed even though it was not transfused.
supporting_points: Blood is often reserved for orthopaedic surgery.
defender.what_would_confirm: The blood-bank issue slip and transfusion record.

judge.rationale: A reservation would be a different charge from transfused units, and nothing documents a transfusion.
judge.counter_argument: The summary states no blood products were given. Please share the transfusion record, or remove {facts.amount_at_stake}.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Can you share the blood-bank issue slip and transfusion record for line L015?

clinical.summary_evidence: physio_documented is false, and the narrative says physiotherapy is not mentioned.
clinical.reasoning: Five billed physiotherapy sessions with no mention in the summary should be supported by session notes.

auditor.claim: Line L016 bills physiotherapy sessions, but the summary records no physiotherapy.
auditor.evidence_point: physio_documented is false and the narrative does not mention it. Amount billed: {facts.amount_at_stake}.
auditor.why_it_matters: Each session should have a therapist's note.

defender.strongest_justification: Early mobilisation after femur fixation is standard, so physiotherapy is likely to have happened.
supporting_points: Physiotherapy after femur surgery is routine.

judge.rationale: Plausible but undocumented. Keep it as a question for the billing desk.
judge.counter_argument: Routine care is still recorded. Please share the session notes, or remove {facts.amount_at_stake}.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: Can you share the physiotherapy session notes for line L016?

clinical.summary_evidence: The portable chest radiograph is not in the structured investigations_documented list.
clinical.reasoning: A billed investigation missing from the structured list is worth checking against the full summary.

auditor.claim: Line L017 bills a portable chest radiograph that is not in the summary's structured investigations list.
auditor.why_it_matters: Billed investigations should be supported by the clinical record.

defender.strongest_justification: The summary narrative states that a portable chest radiograph was obtained in the emergency bay before transfer to the ward.
supporting_points: The free-text summary documents the radiograph explicitly.
It was left out of the structured list only.
defender.what_would_confirm: The radiology report for the emergency-bay chest radiograph.

judge.rationale: The narrative documents the radiograph, so the structured list is incomplete, not the bill.
judge.counter_argument: This charge appears to be explained by the discharge summary narrative, which records the emergency-bay chest radiograph. It is shown for transparency and not counted.
judge.question_for_billing_desk: No question needed: the summary narrative documents this radiograph.
